title: Modal dialog with the native dialog element
when: The user wants a modal window: a confirmation, a short form or a message that blocks the page until answered.
prompt:
Goal: A modal built on <dialog> and showModal() with a title, a close control, a focus trap and focus returned to the trigger.
Steps:
1. <dialog id="confirm" aria-labelledby="confirm-title"> with an h2 title, the content and actions; open it from a <button type="button"> with showModal().
2. Actions in <form method="dialog"> with <button value="cancel">Cancel</button> and <button value="ok">; read dialog.returnValue on close.
3. A visible Close button in the header; Escape works natively.
4. Backdrop click: close when event.target is the dialog itself (wrap content in an inner div).
5. Style ::backdrop translucent dark; width: min(90vw, 32rem); max-height: 85vh with the body scrolling inside.
6. On the close event return focus to the trigger; autofocus the least destructive control.
Quality bar:
- showModal makes the page inert, no hand made trap.
- The title says what is being decided.
- Destructive buttons name the thing (Delete 3 photos).
Pitfalls:
- show() instead of showModal(), leaving the page interactive.
- A div overlay with no Escape.
- A modal on page load before any user action.
Verify:
- [ ] aria-labelledby points at the title.
- [ ] A Close or Cancel control exists.
- [ ] Escape and backdrop click close it.
- [ ] Focus returns to the trigger.
Output: Dialog markup near the end of body, dialog styles in style.css and dialog.js.

examples.input: popup de confirmacao antes de apagar um item
examples.output: dialog aria-labelledby, "Delete this order?" title, form method dialog with Cancel and Delete order, focus back to trigger
